l4_steps.name: Ingest booking & transaction data from PSS
l4_steps.input: Nightly batch feed of PNR, ticketing, and ancillary purchase records
l4_steps.output: Raw booking event stream loaded to data lake
l4_steps.kpi: Data pipeline SLA: 100% of prior-day records ingested by 04:00 local
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PNR schema changes on major releases can silently break field mappings, causing downstream profile gaps until the next data audit cycle

l4_steps.name: Collect loyalty programme interaction events
l4_steps.input: Email opens, loyalty portal logins, miles accrual and redemption events
l4_steps.output: Loyalty event stream appended to data lake
l4_steps.kpi: Event capture rate ≥99% of Salesforce Marketing Cloud triggers per day
l4_steps.pain_point: Loyalty tier change events arrive asynchronously from PSS; without an event-ordering layer, a customer can receive a downgrade communication before the upgrade is confirmed

l4_steps.name: Capture web & mobile behavioural data
l4_steps.input: Clickstream, search, seat-map interaction, and app session events
l4_steps.output: Behavioural event stream with session IDs written to AWS S3
l4_steps.kpi: Tag coverage ≥98% of key conversion pages; session data latency ≤2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: iOS ATT (App Tracking Transparency) and Safari ITP limit cross-device identity stitching, reducing identifiable behavioural profiles by ~20–30% on Apple devices

l4_steps.name: Validate data completeness across all sources
l4_steps.input: Ingested event counts vs expected record volumes per source
l4_steps.output: Completeness scorecard; pipeline held or released
l4_steps.kpi: Overall data completeness ≥95% before downstream processing proceeds
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS-originated bookings (Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus GDS) often arrive with partial passenger profile fields; missing DOB or contact email breaks identity resolution

l4_steps.name: Cleanse and deduplicate customer records
l4_steps.input: Raw multi-source event streams from data lake
l4_steps.kpi: Duplicate record rate ≤0.5% post-cleanse; address standardisation accuracy ≥97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers booking via third-party OTAs (Expedia, booking.com) often have name/email variations that resist standard matching rules, inflating duplicate counts

l4_steps.name: Verify PII consent and GDPR / CCPA compliance
l4_steps.input: Customer consent records, marketing opt-in flags, data retention schedules
l4_steps.output: Consent-cleared record set; non-consented records quarantined
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of records processed against current consent status before any marketing activation; consent sync latency ≤24 hours from collection event
l4_steps.pain_point: Consent revocation must propagate to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, and Braze within the 72-hour GDPR window — cross-system latency routinely misses this SLA without automated orchestration

l4_steps.name: Enforce data retention and right-to-erasure rules
l4_steps.input: Erasure requests from customer portal, regulatory notices
l4_steps.output: Deletion confirmation across all downstream systems within SLA
l4_steps.kpi: Right-to-erasure requests fulfilled within 30 days per GDPR Article 17; 100% completion rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Cascading deletes across Altéa PSS, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, and AWS Redshift require coordinated API calls; partial deletions create residual PII exposure

l4_steps.name: Resolve identity and stitch cross-channel profiles
l4_steps.input: Consent-cleared, cleansed records with email, loyalty ID, device ID, PNR
l4_steps.output: Unified customer profiles with deterministic and probabilistic identity links
l4_steps.kpi: Identity match rate ≥80% of known travellers; profile stitching latency ≤6 hours from data ingestion
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers using travel agent bookings have no direct loyalty ID in the PNR, requiring probabilistic name+route matching which has a ~12% false-positive rate without additional signal

l4_steps.name: Compute customer lifetime value and tier segments
l4_steps.input: Unified profiles enriched with 24-month transaction history
l4_steps.output: CLV score, predicted annual revenue, and tier classification per customer
l4_steps.kpi: CLV model R² ≥0.72; tier classification refreshed weekly; top-decile CLV customers identified for proactive retention
l4_steps.pain_point: Frequent-flyer programme changes (e.g., move from segment- to revenue-based earning) invalidate historical CLV models requiring full retraining — a 3–4 week disruption to personalisation pipelines

l4_steps.name: Run customer segmentation models
l4_steps.input: Unified profiles with CLV, travel frequency, route preferences, ancillary purchase history
l4_steps.output: Customer segment labels (e.g., Leisure Infrequent, Corporate Road Warrior, Premium Aspirant)
l4_steps.kpi: Silhouette score ≥0.55 for k-means clusters; segment refresh cycle ≤7 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Seasonal demand patterns (holidays, school breaks) cause segment drift that is difficult to distinguish from genuine behavioural change — misclassification drives irrelevant offers during peak booking windows

l4_steps.name: Build propensity scores for ancillary and upgrade offers
l4_steps.input: Segment labels, historical ancillary purchase events, seat-map interaction data
l4_steps.output: Per-customer propensity scores: upgrade likelihood, seat upsell, lounge day-pass, travel insurance
l4_steps.kpi: AUC ≥0.75 per propensity model; score refresh ≤48 hours before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Short-haul domestic passengers have sparse ancillary purchase histories, causing propensity models to default to population averages and suppressing personalisation lift on high-frequency leisure routes

l4_steps.name: Score churn risk for loyalty programme members
l4_steps.input: Loyalty transaction recency, frequency, redemption gap, competitive route exposure
l4_steps.output: Churn risk tier (High / Medium / Low) and recommended retention intervention
l4_steps.kpi: Churn model recall ≥70% on held-out validation set; High-risk members flagged ≥60 days before predicted lapse
l4_steps.pain_point: Alliance-free carriers have no partner accrual data to detect cross-airline defection; churn signals are visible only after the customer has already reduced flying frequency, limiting intervention window

l4_steps.name: Generate personalised pre-trip offer packages
l4_steps.input: Propensity scores, segment labels, PNR departure date, fare class booked
l4_steps.output: Personalised offer payload (upgrade, seat, lounge, hotel partner) per customer
l4_steps.kpi: Offer relevance score ≥70% (measured by click-through proxy); ancillary attach rate uplift ≥8% vs control
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO-filed fare class restrictions may invalidate upgrade offers at activation time — without real-time inventory checks against Amadeus NRM, irrelevant offers are served, eroding customer trust

l4_steps.name: Activate offers across email, app push, and web
l4_steps.input: Personalised offer payloads, customer channel preference flags, optimal send-time scores
l4_steps.output: Delivered personalised messages across email, push notification, and website homepage
l4_steps.kpi: Email open rate ≥28%; push notification opt-in rate ≥45%; web personalisation CTR ≥4%
l4_steps.pain_point: Channel fatigue from overlapping CRM, loyalty, and operational email streams — without cross-channel frequency capping in Braze, customers in high-propensity segments receive 5–8 emails per week, driving unsubscribe rates above 0.6%

l4_steps.name: Serve real-time personalisation at airport touchpoints
l4_steps.input: Customer profile, check-in event trigger, real-time upgrade inventory from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Targeted upgrade or ancillary prompt displayed at kiosk or agent terminal
l4_steps.kpi: Kiosk upgrade conversion rate ≥5% for High-propensity customers; offer display latency ≤500ms from check-in event
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time inventory sync between Amadeus Altéa PSS and SITA AMS kiosks can lag by 2–4 minutes during peak check-in, causing declined upgrade offers that had already been verbally accepted at the counter

l4_steps.name: Track offer redemption and revenue attribution
l4_steps.input: Offer delivery logs from Braze and SITA AMS, ancillary revenue from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Offer conversion rate, incremental revenue per segment, cost-per-acquisition
l4_steps.kpi: Incremental ancillary revenue per personalised journey ≥€12 vs control; attribution model updated weekly
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-click attribution in Salesforce Marketing Cloud over-credits email and under-credits app push and airport kiosk touchpoints — multi-touch attribution requires custom AWS Redshift modelling not available out-of-the-box

l4_steps.name: Analyse A/B test results and model performance
l4_steps.input: Conversion data, control vs treatment group outcomes, propensity model predictions vs actuals
l4_steps.output: Performance report; decision to retrain models or adjust segmentation thresholds
l4_steps.kpi: A/B test statistical significance ≥95% before rolling out winning variant; model performance reviewed bi-weekly
l4_steps.pain_point: Small holdout sizes on low-frequency routes (e.g., thin regional services) prevent statistical significance from being reached within a single IATA season, forcing carry-over decisions based on directional data only
